summary.text: Brittany Pettersen is the incumbent U.S. Representative for Colorado's 7th District, first elected in 2022 as the first woman to represent the district. A Jefferson County native, she served a decade in the Colorado legislature before Congress and sits on the House Financial Services Committee. Her official biography says she is focused on mental health and substance use treatment, housing affordability, and consumer protection.

paragraphs.text: Pettersen was born in Colorado and raised in Jefferson County. According to her campaign website, her father was a construction contractor and her mother a hairdresser, and her mother's addiction after being prescribed opioids shaped her interest in behavioral health policy.

She describes herself as the first in her family to graduate from both high school and college. She earned a B.A. in political science from Metropolitan State University of Denver, which her official biography says she paid for by waiting tables.
Before running for office, she worked for New Era Colorado, a nonprofit that works to increase youth participation in politics.

Pettersen served in the Colorado House of Representatives (District 28) from 2013 to 2019. According to her campaign website, she chaired the House Education Committee and passed the Equal Pay for Equal Work Act, a red flag law, and the Secure Savings Act.

She then served in the Colorado State Senate (District 22) from 2019 to 2023, where, her official biography says, her work included legislation on health care costs, the opioid epidemic, reproductive health care, and child care.

In 2022 Pettersen won the open 7th District seat, defeating Republican Erik Aadland with about 56% of the vote. She was re-elected in 2024 over Republican Sergei Matveyuk with about 55%, and was unopposed in the June 30, 2026 Democratic primary.

In the House she serves on the Financial Services Committee, including the Subcommittee on Housing and Insurance, and is Vice Ranking Member of the Subcommittee on National Security, Illicit Finance, and International Financial Institutions, according to her official biography.
The same biography says she lives in Lakewood with her husband, Ian, and their two sons.
